title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — General Assessment #4

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #4
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A kilogram of stones and a kilogram of feathers have the same (1 mark)
   A. Shape
   B. Volume
   C. Mass
   D. Colour

2. What does the stomach do to food? (1 mark)
   A. Churns it and mixes it with juices
   B. Takes back water
   C. Cuts it into pieces
   D. Stores faeces

3. Which project helps you to handle hot pots safely? (1 mark)
   A. Making a dustbin
   B. Making a toy
   C. Making kitchen gloves
   D. Making a poster

4. Which sign of life is shown when a yellow leaf falls from a tree? (1 mark)
   A. Reproducing
   B. Making fruit
   C. Breathing in
   D. Removing waste

5. What instrument measures the volume of a liquid? (1 mark)
   A. Ruler
   B. Stopwatch
   C. Beam balance
   D. Measuring jug

6. Which is an example of reusing? (1 mark)
   A. Throwing it in a drain
   B. Leaving it on the road
   C. Using a washed bottle to carry water
   D. Burning a plastic bottle

7. A plant with no water for many days will (1 mark)
   A. Grow faster
   B. Become weak and may die
   C. Make more flowers
   D. Get stronger

8. Why is waste in rivers dangerous? (1 mark)
   A. It makes water clean
   B. It makes rain
   C. It makes water dirty and harms fish
   D. It makes fish bigger

9. Which of these is a way of storing leftover food safely? (1 mark)
   A. Sharing it with flies
   B. Putting it on the floor
   C. Leaving it uncovered in the sun
   D. Covering it and keeping it clean

10. Which of these is NOT a source of light? (1 mark)
   A. A candle
   B. An electric bulb
   C. A torch
   D. A mirror

11. Which of these is a sign of life in animals? (1 mark)
   A. Staying in one place forever
   B. Being made of metal
   C. Being painted
   D. Feeding

12. Which part of a bean plant grows in the soil? (1 mark)
   A. Roots
   B. Leaves
   C. Pods
   D. Flowers

13. Which of these is NOT matter? (1 mark)
   A. Milk
   B. Light from a torch
   C. Air
   D. A stone

14. The touch-me-not plant folds its leaves when touched. This shows that plants can (1 mark)
   A. move from place to place
   B. respond to changes
   C. eat food
   D. lay eggs

15. What is decomposable waste? (1 mark)
   A. Waste that rots and breaks down
   B. Waste made of plastic
   C. Waste that never changes
   D. Waste made of metal

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Describe how a poster can teach the community about water conservation. Give four features. (4 marks)

17. Discuss how the three Rs can be used for waste from a school kitchen. (5 marks)

18. Give two examples each of vertebrates and invertebrates, and state one feature of each group. (4 marks)

19. Why is chewing food well important? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #4 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Mass
   Both are 1 kg. The feathers take up much more space.

2. A — Churns it and mixes it with juices
   The stomach churns food into a thick soup with digestive juices.

3. C — Making kitchen gloves
   Gloves protect hands.

4. D — Removing waste
   Old leaves may carry waste away when they fall.

5. D — Measuring jug
   A measuring jug or cylinder shows volume.

6. C — Using a washed bottle to carry water
   The bottle is used again for a new purpose.

7. B — Become weak and may die
   Water is needed for life, so a plant without it wilts and may die.

8. C — It makes water dirty and harms fish
   Waste pollutes water and harms living things.

9. D — Covering it and keeping it clean
   Covered food is safer from germs.

10. D — A mirror
   A mirror only reflects light.

11. D — Feeding
   Animals feed, grow, breathe, reproduce, remove waste, move, respond and die.

12. A — Roots
   Roots grow underground.

13. B — Light from a torch
   Light has no mass and takes up no space.

14. B — respond to changes
   Folding when touched is a response to a change in the surroundings.

15. A — Waste that rots and breaks down
   Decomposable waste is broken down by decomposers.

SECTION B
----
16. (4 marks)
   Answer: A clear message, big pictures, short slogan, bright colours, ideas for saving water, placed where many people see it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four features.

17. (5 marks)
   Answer: Reduce: cook and serve only what is needed. Reuse: use empty oil tins for storage and sacks for carrying. Recycle: sell scrap metal and paper, compost peelings.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each R, 1 mark for one clear example and 1 mark for the compost point.

18. (4 marks)
   Answer: Vertebrates: goat and tilapia, have a backbone. Invertebrates: ant and snail, have no backbone.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two vertebrates, 1 mark for feature, 1 mark for two invertebrates, 1 mark for feature.

19. (2 marks)
   Answer: It breaks food into small pieces and makes digestion easier.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for small pieces and 1 mark for easier digestion.
